flags: SHAP describes what the model does, not what causes bankruptcy. A large contribution is a model pattern, not a cause.

Correlated ratios split credit, so one ratio can look less important because a close twin shares its signal. Known near twins: Attr2 and Attr17 (exact reciprocals), Attr9 and Attr36 (near duplicates). Category sums are only a partial remedy.

The five categories are assigned by this project from each formula. They are not in the UCI description or the dictionary. Borderline cases are Attr27, Attr30, Attr33, Attr34, Attr37 and Attr58. The full map is in the appendix.

3 of the 10 most important features have UNVERIFIED definitions (Attr24, Attr38, Attr13). Read their plain-language names as the UCI wording, which the dictionary marks as possibly mistranslated, unclear or inconsistent.
Importance stability: Spearman correlation of mean |SHAP| between train and validation is 0.999, and 10 of the top 10 features agree. Agreement with LightGBM gain importance (Spearman) is 0.831.

Cross-checks: SHAP additivity error against the model output is at most 2.1e-14. The shap library differs from LightGBM's native contributions by at most 0.0e+00; a difference of exactly zero suggests the library delegates to LightGBM's own routine for this model type, so that comparison is not an independent check.
The frozen model is refit on all of train, while the Platt slope was fitted on fold models. The slope is applied to the refit model. Whether that mismatch matters is not verified.
The base value is the model's average output over the training trees, not the observed bankruptcy rate, so it need not equal the prevalence.
Example firms were chosen by a rule fixed in advance, and there is no company id, so they are identified by validation row number.
Validation has 61 bankrupt firms and importance is an average over all 878 firms. The intervals show the sampling noise.
Test split untouched in this phase.

In 2 of the 3 example firms (highest_scoring_true_positive, highest_scoring_false_alarm) the largest driver is Attr21 being missing. The model gives such firms a very large score on that signal alone.
Attr21 missing vs present SHAP: mean abs SHAP is 5.190 when missing vs 0.322 when present (validation; 12 firms have it missing). Pattern only.
Attr21 train: bankruptcy rate 0.973 when missing (73 firms) vs 0.053 when present (4021 firms); the 95% Wilson intervals do not overlap. Pattern only.
Attr21 val: bankruptcy rate 0.917 when missing (12 firms) vs 0.058 when present (866 firms); the 95% Wilson intervals do not overlap. Pattern only.
